prerequisites: Vector analysis, differential and integral calculus of several variables, curve and surface integrals, ordinary differential equations, basics of compressible and incompressible as well as frictionless and viscous flows, Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, shock wave. Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Entrance and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of advanced technical and methodological knowledge in Fluid Mechanics.
Acquisition of a deeper physical understanding of important flow phenomena.
Acquisition of mathematical approaches for solving important classes of flow problems.
Present advanced technical and methodological knowledge in Fluid Mechanics in a structured way and explain flow phenomena comprehensibly.
Confidently apply mathematical approaches to solve important classes of flow problems and methodically perform the non-dimensionalization of balance equations.
Comprehensibly explain essential concepts of lubrication theory as well as vorticity, streamlines, and vortex transport, and concisely describe turbulence phenomena.
Present potential flows in a structured manner.
Reliably calculate the drag of slender bodies.
Concise explanation of d'Alembert's paradox.
Present the Blasius solution in a structured manner.
Systematically distinguish boundary layers.
Clearly explain separation processes.
Clearly present the RANS equations, comprehensibly explain approaches for modeling Reynolds stresses.
Purposefully apply the wall law for turbulent pipe flows.
Independently, comprehensibly, and reproducibly solve exercise problems.
Formulate one's own thoughts and calculations in an audience-appropriate manner.
Constructively discuss work progress and feedback from exercises with peers, for example in partner and group work.
Systematically investigate observed sources of error in solutions.
Concise summarization of content, e.g., theoretical foundations.
Purposefully plan exam preparation with respect to time and resources and structured processing of calculation examples and theoretical questions in written exams.

syllabus_topics: Non-dimensionalization of balance equations, creeping flow (Stokes problem)
Lubrication theory, vorticity, streamlines, and vortex transport equation
Potential flows, drag of a slender body, d'Alembert's paradox

Blasius solution, separation and classification of boundary layers, turbulence phenomena, Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes equations, modeling of Reynolds stresses and the wall law (turbulent pipe flow)
teaching_methods: Lecture on the theoretical foundations and applications of the above-mentioned chapters
Practicing what has been learned by independently solving exercise problems

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with calculation examples and theoretical questions
Regular homework, board performance, tests (possible performance checks)

assessment_rules: A written exam with calculation examples and theoretical questions will be conducted. Performance checks through regular homework, board performance, and tests are possible. Specific examination modalities are to be provided in the study information system before the start of the semester.
